_comment: Permissions for the zebra vetting agents. Tracked in git on purpose: it
authorises exactly the commands the prompt templates in zebra/config.py
tell agents to type, so the two can never drift apart.
WHY THIS FILE IS LOAD-BEARING: agents are spawned with `claude -p`, which
is non-interactive. A tool with no matching allow rule is DENIED outright,
not prompted. Without this the agents start, get refused on their first
`zebra vet show`, and die without landing a verdict — every signal enters
unvetted while the switch still reads ON. (The health watchdog now catches
that shape via `spawns_since_landing`, but do not rely on the alarm to
discover a permissions problem you can prevent here.)
SCOPE IS DELIBERATELY NARROW. The agents may run the READ and DECIDE verbs
and nothing else. A broad `Bash(python:*)` would also authorise `zebra
close`, `zebra enter` and `zebra reset --confirm` — i.e. it would hand the
model the power to open and close positions, which is precisely the
invariant the whole layer is built to preserve. Keep it narrow: an agent
that needs a new verb should get a new line here, reviewed.
PATHS: the Pi runs the bot under CROCODILE/venv. If that interpreter path
ever changes, these rules stop matching and the agents go silent — update
both here and in the deploy notes.
